status: Desk research and provisional specification. No live runtime, billing, extraction or isolation proof performed.
purpose: One maintained research program for Provider-created bounded services, optional managed operation, direct/market distribution and a prospective Provider-as-Seller fiat lane; current AE principal-reseller entry preserved.

evidence_rules.documented: Published technical/pricing/terms contract; behavior not exercised.
evidence_rules.source-inspected: Specific source code examined at commit or installed dependency; not executed.
evidence_rules.observed: Requires recorded live input/output; none in this study.

sources.title: Automat Ace
sources.locator: Meet Ace; published 2026-09-30
sources.finding: Own computer and persistent identity; FDE setup and maintenance. Full page fetch unavailable; infrastructure unknown.

sources.title: Meta Muse launch
sources.locator: Dedicated VM; Sentinel; privacy

sources.title: Muse security architecture
sources.locator: Runtime cell; privsep; hatch-authd; Sentinel; capabilities; browser broker
sources.finding: Credential and durable state domains are separate from the agent runtime. Host-side approval and egress checks cover concrete requests.

sources.title: Muse product design
sources.locator: Agent experience; approvals
sources.finding: Persistent personal context; structured UI for consent and credentials.

sources.title: Grok Bot overview
sources.locator: Your bots and their shared computer
sources.finding: A user’s bots share the same computer, files, browser sessions and app logins.

sources.title: Grok Bot security
sources.locator: Updated 2026-09-28; enterprise policies; credentials; deletion; residency
sources.finding: Enterprise controls differ from self-serve Teams. Bot deletion does not delete shared computer state. Connector credentials stay outside the computer.

sources.title: OpenAI Dots launch
sources.locator: Personal dots and organizational specialist dots
sources.finding: Always-on assistants plus focused organizational pilots, including invoice/procurement workflows. A public ephemeral deployment API was not established.

sources.title: Dots safety architecture
sources.locator: Action checks; isolated workspaces; sign-in
sources.finding: Layered action checks and controlled workspaces; not a public description of the complete infrastructure stack.

sources.title: Instinct product
sources.locator: Personal agent capabilities
sources.finding: Proactive personal assistant across phone, computer and personal channels; broad persistent context.

sources.title: Instinct privacy
sources.locator: AI training; opt-out; safety exceptions; deletion
sources.finding: Training opt-out has exceptions; disconnecting an integration is distinct from deleting previously stored information.

sources.title: Instinct terms
sources.locator: Actions; appointment; Materials; account use
sources.finding: Broad authority to perform actions and bind third-party agreements; unsuitable as the default authority model for a bounded task service.

sources.title: OpenMuse README
sources.locator: L68 runtime setup; L150 single owner; L174 isolation; L182 retries; L186 dependencies; L223 adapter
sources.finding: Single-owner reference application, MIT source. Persistent browser/workspace; CopilotKit service dependency; OpenBot bridge described as unfinished.

sources.title: OpenMuse authentication
sources.locator: L23-59 sessions and signed file access
sources.finding: Expiring hashed session tokens and signed file access; owner identity is not tenant-isolation proof.

sources.title: OpenMuse action execution
sources.locator: L40-95 proposal; L103-150 approval/claim; L169-188 outcome
sources.finding: Stable action identity, connection-version approval checks, atomic execution claim and explicit uncertain outcomes.

sources.title: OpenMuse task worker
sources.locator: L118-150 leases/CAS; L170-174 heartbeat; L196 checkpoint
sources.finding: Lease and compare-and-swap state updates fence stale workers and persist checkpoints.

sources.title: OpenMuse computer isolation
sources.locator: L113-123 owner/deployment identity; L263-286 configuration checks
sources.finding: Rejects mismatched container networking, mounts and resource configuration. Not a demonstrated multi-tenant VM security boundary.

sources.title: OpenMuse browser worker limits
sources.locator: L3 worker token; L53 session limits; L64 browser/security caveats
sources.finding: Worker token remains server-side; application network checks are not a kernel firewall, and browser sandbox limitations are acknowledged.

sources.title: OpenMuse OpenBot adapter
sources.locator: Authenticated transport and disabled adapter contract
sources.finding: Per-person transport and upstream authority checks; not evidence of a production-ready bridge.

sources.title: E2B pricing
sources.locator: Pro subscription; concurrency extensions; CPU and RAM rates
sources.finding: Running compute metered by CPU/RAM seconds; Pro subscription and capacity extensions are additional. Listed $ currency treated as USD pending confirmation.

sources.title: E2B billing and quotas
sources.locator: Running usage; create rate; Pro limits
sources.finding: Running time is billable; paused/killed compute stops. Pro creation quota is 5/s per project; admission must handle 429 responses.

sources.title: E2B persistence
sources.locator: Pause/resume; timeout; snapshot failures; pause/resume performance; paused retention
sources.finding: Full pause preserves disk/RAM; docs estimate ~4 seconds/GiB to pause and ~1 second to resume. Paused state persists until explicit deletion. API latency is not a measured billed duration.

sources.title: E2B network access
sources.locator: Default access; allowlists; DNS exception; shared domains; updateNetwork
sources.finding: Network defaults require restriction. Domain policies involve DNS exceptions and shared destinations; changing policy can widen access.

sources.title: E2B external proxy
sources.locator: Private beta; host TCP enforcement; DNS path
sources.finding: Host proxy can restrict TCP and fail closed, but documented DNS traffic uses a separate path. Requires testing, not a claimed exploit.

sources.title: E2B workload identity
sources.locator: Private beta; JWT-SVID; scopes and audiences
sources.finding: Workload identity is promising for a job gateway but is private beta and cannot be a required GA dependency yet.

sources.title: E2B volumes limitations
sources.locator: Private beta; read-only mounts; permissions; regions
sources.finding: Volume limitations do not support assuming a read-only per-folder boundary. External artifact storage is the proposed baseline.

sources.title: E2B terms
sources.locator: Restrictions; modified 2024-12-04
sources.finding: Providing access/resale is restricted absent written authorization. Embedded commercial job execution needs contractual clarification.

sources.title: Composio pricing
sources.locator: New accounts from 2026-08-15; own OAuth; Pro credits; ZDR add-on
sources.finding: Own OAuth has free tool-call allowance; Pro is a credit commitment. Managed OAuth, triggers and optional features have different meters.

sources.title: Composio sessions
sources.locator: Toolkit/tool allowlists; metatools; connected accounts
sources.finding: A session needs explicit allowlists and account selection. Tool catalog narrowing does not itself enforce business argument constraints.

sources.title: Composio Xero toolkit
sources.locator: Authentication and supported actions
sources.finding: Xero requires the developer’s own OAuth configuration. Raw create-invoice tools are broader than the proposed draft-bill action.

sources.title: Composio ZDR scope
sources.locator: Covered requests; excluded files, triggers, sandbox and search; enablement
sources.finding: ZDR does not cover staged files, retained trigger payloads or certain offloaded responses. Own OAuth and explicit project enablement matter.

sources.title: Composio terms
sources.locator: Section 3 License Grant; Section 8 content; Section 13 co-marketing
sources.finding: Commercial-use grant conflicts with restrictive resale/commercial-use wording. Embedded use and data license need written clarification.

sources.title: Nango tool calling
sources.locator: Actions; credentials; selected tool functions
sources.finding: Auth and server-side integration functions can back a typed action gateway. Do not expose a general API proxy to the guest.

sources.title: Nango security
sources.locator: Encryption; deletion; logs; retention
sources.finding: Vaulted credentials; deletion and log retention are separate. Immediate inaccessibility is distinct from subsequent hard deletion.

sources.title: Nango pricing
sources.locator: PAYG commitment; connections; compute; egress
sources.finding: PAYG commitment includes credits, with separate connection, compute and transfer rates. Conservative model does not assume free-tier allowances carry over.

sources.title: Nango terms and DPA
sources.locator: Sections 3, 5, 8, 12; DPA
sources.finding: Product-integration purpose, USD fees and customer-data processing license; access-transfer restrictions remain a service-order question.

sources.title: Convex pricing
sources.locator: Professional resource table; US East 1.0x
sources.finding: Seats plus resource overages: functions, action compute, storage, database I/O and data egress. Regional multiplier must be confirmed.

sources.title: Convex regions
sources.locator: Available regions
sources.finding: Sydney is currently available. Database location alone does not locate sandboxes, model inference or connector subprocessors.

sources.title: Convex file authorization
sources.locator: Storage URLs and HTTP actions
sources.finding: Direct file URLs grant access to their holder; use an authorization check for each protected download rather than assume URL secrecy is revocation.

sources.title: Installed Convex workflow contract
sources.locator: Cancellation; determinism; events; workpool; payload limits
sources.finding: Cancellation cannot undo an already-running action. Live workflow changes require versioning; durable waits allow releasing runtime compute.

sources.title: OpenRouter model price snapshot
sources.locator: data entries openai/gpt-6-luna and openai/gpt-6.1-sol; pricing.prompt/completion
sources.finding: Per-token prices read 2026-10-01; no extraction-quality tests. Mutable model IDs are not immutable model-weight pins.

sources.title: OpenRouter retention controls
sources.locator: Provider eligibility; inference-only scope
sources.finding: Route only to eligible inference providers; tool/search providers have separate retention policies.

sources.title: OpenRouter Business and fees
sources.locator: Credit fees; regional routing; DPA; exclusions
sources.finding: Standard credit fee 5.5%, Business 8%. Business region routing supports US/EU; no suitable provider fails instead of leaving region.

sources.title: Stripe Australia pricing
sources.locator: Domestic cards; Billing pay-as-you-go
sources.finding: Domestic card pricing and subscription Billing are separate charges; model assumes monthly domestic-card collection, excluding GST.

sources.title: Xero developer FAQ
sources.locator: 2026 API tiers; granular scopes; egress; AI and automation restrictions
sources.finding: API subscription depends on connected organizations. Training on API data is prohibited; approved API workflow is the proposed access path.

sources.title: Xero idempotent requests
sources.locator: Idempotency-Key documentation; six-minute lifetime; key re-use and failure behavior
sources.finding: Xero documents idempotency-key expiry six minutes after first request. Endpoint coverage and late-resume reconciliation require live tests; a new key after an uncertain write risks duplicates.

sources.title: ACCC small-business contracts
sources.locator: Unfair contract terms; small-business coverage
sources.finding: Standard-form business contracts may have unfair-terms protections; counsel must review one-sided risk allocation.

sources.title: ACCC service guarantees
sources.locator: Services; due care; fitness; timing
sources.finding: Applicable guarantees can constrain blanket disclaimers. No legal determination of this proposed offering has been made.

sources.title: OAIC overseas personal information
sources.locator: APP 8; use versus disclosure; accountability
sources.finding: Assess the whole processing chain and contractual control, not just primary database residency.

sources.title: Google Workspace developer data policy
sources.locator: Limited Use and restricted-scope developer policy
sources.finding: OAuth verification and permitted downstream data uses need task-specific review. This study does not assert application approval.

sources.title: Tasklet guide
sources.locator: Agent folders and workspace behavior; prior dated research
sources.finding: Packaging reference for workflow setup. Not relied on for embedded runtime API availability or current price.

sources.title: Pickaxe actions
sources.locator: Connections and end-user accounts; prior dated comparison archive
sources.finding: Packaging reference for connecting user accounts. No claim of task-level isolation from an action picker.

sources.title: Superlayer product and beta pricing
sources.locator: Realtime database, built-in features, pricing and open source
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: Backend on the InstantDB engine; listed $25/month beta pricing shares usage across unlimited apps. It is not documented here as a VM execution service.

sources.title: Superlayer platform provisioning
sources.locator: Temporary apps; long-lived apps; token scoping
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: Programmatic app/schema/permission provisioning; temporary apps expire after two weeks. App-scoped admin tokens can change that app’s permissions and remain too powerful for a task worker.

sources.title: Superlayer permissions
sources.locator: Namespaces; default permissions; attrs; newData
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: Ordinary data permissions default to allow unless overridden. Explicit default-deny and schema-change restrictions are required for a bounded-worker design.

sources.title: Superlayer backend SDK
sources.locator: Admin SDK; impersonation; permissions
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: Admin queries/writes bypass permission checks; asUser applies user rules. Keep admin credentials outside the guest and validate service operations separately.

sources.title: Superlayer streams
sources.locator: How Streams work; permissions; serverless waitUntil
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: Streams are storage-backed and do not expire automatically; stream permissions default deny. Persisted streams are not proof of durable job or side-effect execution.

sources.title: Superlayer webhooks
sources.locator: Signature; idempotency keys; delivery and retries
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: Signed notifications have stable redelivery keys, retries, a 15-second delivery timeout and failure disablement. Acknowledge after durable admission rather than run a task in the handler.

sources.title: Superlayer transaction semantics
sources.locator: Transacts are atomic; typesafety
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: Atomic multi-operation commits are documented. Conditional lease/budget admission and fencing under contention were not established by the pages reviewed.

sources.title: E2B auto-resume policy
sources.locator: Supported wake operations; Cleanup
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: File/command/service activity can wake a paused sandbox. Each auto-resume uses a timeout of at least five minutes; this is not a minimum billable duration if explicitly paused sooner.

sources.title: E2B filesystem-only standby
sources.locator: Full vs filesystem-only; resume behavior; validation
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: Disk-only snapshots discard RAM and restart processes on resume. Published qualitative performance is faster/lighter, not a measured latency in this study.

sources.title: E2B fork behavior
sources.locator: Fork flow and state preservation
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: Fork copies disk and memory into independent sandboxes. Customer data, running processes and stale job capabilities may also be copied; cross-tenant golden images must be clean.

sources.title: E2B secured controller access
sources.locator: Secured access; X-Access-Token
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: Controller calls require a sandbox access token when secured access is enabled. This does not establish authorization-before-wake behavior for every exposed service route.

sources.title: Superlayer permission rate limits
sources.locator: Token bucket; per entity limits
sources.access_method: Public HTML read directly; web index/fetch unavailable for Superlayer
sources.finding: Permission rules can apply keyed rate limits. These are not a replacement for monetary reservations or runtime/provider capacity admission.

sources.title: Cloudflare agent lifecycle
sources.locator: What survives; recovery; asynchronous operations
sources.finding: Durable identity, SQL, schedules and checkpoints survive hibernation; RAM variables and open requests do not. This is not E2B memory-snapshot semantics.

sources.title: Cloudflare current sandbox environments
sources.locator: Overview; Containers; Dynamic Workers; updated 2026-09-30
sources.finding: Linux Container instances are dedicated microVMs; Durable Object scheduling is public beta. Dynamic Workers isolate generated code and expose only supplied methods/data. Current docs distinguish SDK 1.0 from 0.x.

sources.title: Cloudflare sandbox credential boundary
sources.locator: Credentials and network access; updated 2026-09-30
sources.finding: Keep tokens in host Worker. Containers with Internet disabled reach intercepted hostnames; Dynamic Workers with globalOutbound null cannot make their own network requests. Application-specific method/body/resource authorization remains our responsibility.

sources.title: Cloudflare Container pricing
sources.locator: vCPU, memory, disk; instance types; egress; Workers/DO/log charges
sources.finding: US$5 paid plan has allowances. CPU billed on active usage; memory/disk on provisioned resources while running. Additional Workers, Durable Objects, logs and regional egress charges; not an apples-to-apples E2B replacement.

sources.title: Cloudflare Workflow pricing
sources.locator: Pricing dimensions; steps and storage billing; updated 2026-09-21
sources.finding: CPU, invocations, steps and retained state are metered. Idle/waiting does not incur Workflow CPU; completed and waiting state still counts as storage. Current step/storage billing began 2026-08-10.

sources.title: Cloudflare Durable Object transaction boundary
sources.locator: SQL transactions; transactionSync; private per-object storage
sources.finding: SQLite-backed objects support synchronous atomic transactions with rollback on thrown errors. This is a local object transaction, not a cross-object or remote-SaaS transaction.

sources.title: Cloudflare Outbound Worker coverage
sources.locator: Use Outbound Workers; final Note
sources.finding: Outbound Workers mediate user-Worker fetches and disable its connect API, but do not intercept fetches from Durable Objects or mTLS bindings. Documented exclusion; no exploit observed.

sources.title: Cloudflare Web Bot Auth
sources.locator: Request component selection; section 4.3 nonce limitation; transitive trust; checked 2026-10-01
sources.finding: Signs selected request components. Cloudflare currently does not validate nonce or track seen nonces for replay protection; it recommends short expiry. Operator/end-user Forwarded trust is experimental. Our mutation boundary needs its own payload binding and durable deduplication.

sources.title: A2A v1 protocol trust responsibilities
sources.locator: Sections 7.5; 7.6.4; 8.4; 13.1; v1 overview checked 2026-10-01
sources.finding: Per-request authorization is server responsibility; in-task authorization does not define scope, representation, validity or revocation semantics. Agent Card signatures are optional. A task completion report does not independently verify our service contract.

sources.title: MCP current security best practices
sources.locator: Confused deputy; token passthrough; SSRF; state-handle hijacking
sources.finding: Validate intended token audience and caller-owned state handles, avoid token passthrough, and protect discovery/outbound URLs against SSRF. A state handle or tool description does not establish authority.

sources.title: OAuth token exchange and actor identity
sources.locator: Sections 1; 2; 4.1 act claim
sources.finding: Token exchange supports delegation and target audience/resource. Current actor and top-level claims govern authorization; nested prior act claims are informational, not inherited access rights.

sources.title: OAuth Rich Authorization Requests
sources.locator: Sections 1; 2; authorization_details
sources.finding: Structured authorization_details can describe fine-grained actions/resources; authorization and resource servers must implement/enforce the profile. It is not universally supported by connected SaaS apps.

sources.title: Auth0 Token Vault
sources.locator: FAQ: user flow; token security; access-token retrieval
sources.finding: Manages third-party consent, storage, refresh and token retrieval. Its described flow returns a short-lived access token to the calling application/agent; our design must keep that token in trusted action code rather than assume vaulting alone contains it.

sources.title: AP2 current payment authorization specification
sources.locator: Mandates; modes; deterministic verification; extension points
sources.finding: Checkout and payment mandates bind authorization to purchase/payment facts with deterministic verification. Execution permissions and service output validation remain separate. Current terminology differs from older Intent/Cart summaries.

sources.title: AP2 security threat model
sources.locator: Security considerations; manipulated checkout
sources.finding: The protocol assumes preventing prompt injection is infeasible and includes agents/LLMs as potential attackers; mandate binding prevents substitution. This is a useful containment premise, not proof of our implementation.

sources.title: Visa Trusted Agent Protocol
sources.locator: Introduction; trust model; agent recognition signature
sources.finding: Participating merchants can recognize approved agent traffic and consumer/payment context with signatures. Merchants may not adopt it. Program recognition does not independently establish our business-service obligations or delivery quality.

sources.title: ABN Lookup verification limits
sources.locator: Active/cancelled ABN; update frequency; contact details
sources.finding: Public registration status and entity information are available, but accuracy/currency/completeness are not guaranteed. Proposed controller/key verification and task-quality checks are separate from registration lookup.

sources.title: OAIC APP 8 contractor disclosure
sources.locator: Paragraphs 8.12-8.17; contractor/subcontractor and contractual safeguards
sources.finding: For applicable APP entities, overseas contractor access is usually disclosure, with limited use exceptions. Guidance describes enforceable contractual safeguards and circumstance-dependent accountability. Actual offer applicability needs legal assessment.

sources.title: ACCC business purchases and consumer guarantees
sources.locator: When consumer rights apply; Business use
sources.finding: Businesses can qualify as consumers, including qualifying purchases below A$100,000 including GST, with exceptions. B2B labeling does not by itself remove applicable guarantees; actual arrangement needs review.

sources.title: Cloudflare current sandbox lifetime
sources.locator: Stopped Container; keeping files; updated current SDK docs
sources.finding: Container filesystem is transient unless explicitly snapshotted; Container stop and Durable Object hibernation are different lifecycles. No snapshot/deletion/billing behavior exercised.

sources.title: Toyo current product site
sources.locator: Executive assistant; integrations; data-location FAQ
sources.finding: Messaging/voice executive assistant with connected business apps. Current public site does not disclose a complete runtime design or a reproducible 1000x cost benchmark.

sources.title: Toyo organizational environment terms
sources.locator: Updated 6 May 2026; sections 1, 2, 3.3 and 4
sources.finding: Published terms describe a shared organizational VM/workspace and agents acting on the Customer behalf. This wording does not establish the topology of the later Worker-based architecture claim or fit our independent Provider obligations.

sources.title: Cloudflare experimental shell package
sources.locator: Experimental notice; What it is; What it is not; durable Workspace example
sources.finding: Typed JavaScript filesystem operations with SQLite/optional R2 durability. Not Bash or Linux process execution. Repository package metadata says 0.4.3; no package installation or runtime test performed.

sources.title: Cloudflare workspace storage implementation
sources.locator: WorkspaceOptions lines 96-115; constructor 236-298; R2 prefix/key 377-390; writeFile 728-825; writeFileStream 906-934
sources.finding: Inline default 1,500,000 bytes. R2 prefix falls back to name and throws when unavailable; global uniqueness remains application responsibility. Large writes put R2 content before SQL metadata and attempt cleanup on SQL failure. Stream writes buffer content; no runtime or concurrency proof.

sources.title: Cloudflare Dynamic Worker billing
sources.locator: Daily creation identity; rates; invocation and startup CPU accounting
sources.finding: Daily distinct code/ID combinations incur creation charges beyond the monthly allowance; no-ID load counts per invocation. Stable get IDs reduce repeated counts. CPU includes startup; Workers allowances are shared. Published rates only.

sources.title: Cloudflare R2 storage and operation pricing
sources.locator: Updated 1 October 2026; Standard rates; free tier; rounding
sources.finding: Standard storage and operation charges persist independently of running compute; direct R2 egress is free. Free monthly allowances and billable-unit rounding apply. Not a zero-total-idle-cost guarantee.

sources.title: Dynamic Worker application assets
sources.locator: Runtime assets; loader-side binding; buildAssetManifest
sources.finding: A Dynamic Worker can serve generated application code and static assets supplied through host bindings backed by KV/R2. This does not imply Linux process compatibility or a continuously running server.

sources.title: Dynamic Worker network and binding boundary
sources.locator: Updated 29 September 2026; block outbound; bindings; host gateway
sources.finding: globalOutbound null blocks guest fetch/connect; explicitly passed bindings remain accessible. Our scoped file and business-action authorization must constrain those bindings. Not exercised.

sources.title: Stripe Australia Connect pricing
sources.locator: Stripe handles pricing vs platform handles pricing
sources.finding: Direct model can place processing fees with connected business; platform-priced model adds A$2 per active account-month and 0.25% plus A$0.25 per payout. Do not apply these to every Call or assume partner revenue share.

sources.title: Stripe Connect risk ownership
sources.locator: Direct and indirect charges; negative balances
sources.finding: Direct charge connected account is merchant of record in Stripe terminology; indirect charges expose platform balances. Connected-account losses depend on configuration; platform retains its own losses and non-payment obligations.

sources.title: Stripe direct charges
sources.locator: Connected-account scope; application-fee refunds
sources.finding: Charge and payment objects are connected-account scoped. Refunding a charge does not automatically refund application fees; explicitly return the agreed fee and reconcile async events.

sources.title: Stripe machine payments
sources.locator: MPP, x402; payment methods; availability
sources.finding: MPP supports shared-payment-token cards and stablecoins; x402 is a stablecoin option. Card SPT minimum US$0.50; stablecoin minimum USDC0.01. Eligibility and session settlement differ by method and country.

sources.title: Stripe shared payment tokens seller availability
sources.locator: Supported countries; scoped grant; preview terms
sources.finding: Listed US, Canada and selected European countries omit Australia on study date. Grant binds seller profile, amount/currency and expiry; no Australian SPT launch availability assumed.

sources.title: Stripe MPP integration
sources.locator: PaymentIntent; card and stablecoin paths; Connect fee payer
sources.finding: MPP is a protocol, Tempo a separate stablecoin-chain route. Stripe hosted fee-payer sponsorship does not support Connect; qualified payment method and commercial topology are still required.

sources.title: Stripe authorization holds
sources.locator: capture_before; card validity windows
sources.finding: Holds expire; common online windows are five/seven days with exact deadline reported on the charge. Not an indefinite escrow or guarantee of service acceptance.

sources.title: Stripe refunds
sources.locator: Original processing fees; pending/failed refunds; events
sources.finding: Original processing fees are retained on refunds. Insufficient balances can leave card refunds pending, other methods can fail. Refund requested is not refund succeeded.

sources.title: Airwallex Payments for Platforms
sources.locator: Connected accounts; gateway or PSP agnostic; split and reconciliation
sources.finding: Actual embedded collection/payout product, distinct from AgentOS. Product capabilities and commercial approval depend on platform fund flow; no applicable embedded quote obtained.

sources.title: Airwallex split settlement
sources.locator: Standard settlement; manual release; reverse splits
sources.finding: Manual release documented for platform-owned and connected-account-owned payments; refunds/chargebacks can require reverse split. Not treated as licensed escrow or automatic transfer of service liability.

sources.title: Airwallex AgentOS
sources.locator: OAuth MCP; read/write scope; money-out defaults; injection guidance
sources.finding: Financial account operations rather than service-commerce contract. Production MCP has no money-out by default; client authorization, write approvals and prompt-injection concerns remain.

sources.title: Airwallex connected account regions
sources.locator: Country table; onboarding vs capability coverage
sources.finding: Indexed first-party documentation lists Australia and distinguishes onboarding from capabilities. Current page fetch empty; actual platform approval, jurisdiction and products remain unresolved.

sources.title: ASIC non-cash payment relief 2026
sources.locator: Instrument 2026/167; relief through April 2031
sources.finding: Current conditional relief replaces 2016/211. Does not establish AE licensing exemption; actual facility and payment reforms require qualified assessment.

sources.title: ATO crypto assets used in business
sources.locator: Trading stock or investment
sources.finding: Ordinary-course business exchange and investment holdings have different tax treatment. A universal CGT-event-per-Call claim is not supported.

sources.title: ATO GST Australian consumer classification
sources.locator: Paragraphs 10–12 and 93; business recipient declarations
sources.finding: GST-registered enterprise acquisitions differ from Australian consumer acquisitions for inbound intangibles. EDP classification and invoice/credit entitlement require actual attributed facts.

sources.title: Harvey Spaces
sources.locator: Self-serve AI delivery; workflows into client Spaces
sources.finding: Firms can deploy workflows/playbooks to clients. Adjacent Provider enablement already exists; no open cross-harness purchasing or economics observed.

sources.title: Thomson Reuters CoCounsel in Claude
sources.locator: 12 May 2026 partnership announcement
sources.finding: Specialist professional capabilities reach a buyer harness through an integration. Cross-harness specialist supply is contested, not an uncontested AE category.

sources.title: Stripe payment sharing across direct-charge sellers
sources.locator: SetupIntent; clone supported types; country authentication; updates
sources.finding: Payment methods are not automatically shared across sellers. Cards and US bank accounts can be cloned; country/SCA setup and independent copies need handling. No generic PayTo cloning assumed.

sources.title: Stripe Accounts v2 configuration
sources.locator: Merchant configuration; fees_collector; losses_collector; dashboard
sources.finding: Configure commercial responsibilities explicitly; some settings cannot be changed later. Full dashboard and Stripe fee/loss collection are the provisional direct-charge choice; capabilities must be checked.

sources.title: The Bid Agency tender and bid reviews
sources.locator: Review process; Pricing Guide
sources.level: first-party documented offer; no transaction or demand verification
sources.finding: Supplier advertises criterion/compliance/evidence review, marked-up PDF and written findings; small-tender guide starts A$1,500 ex GST and includes meetings. Establishes an existing paid service category, not demand for our narrower offer or platform.

sources.title: TenderWise tender review service
sources.locator: Free initial high-level review; detailed paid review
sources.level: first-party documented offer; no transaction verification
sources.finding: Free initial high-level review competes with shallow screening; detailed assessment is a paid fixed-fee offer. Selected pilot must provide a substantive scoped review rather than charge for a generic summary.

sources.title: Public Tenders Australia review offer
sources.locator: Search-indexed engagement snapshot and BidCaddy portal description
sources.level: first-party search-indexed only; full open returned no body
sources.finding: Advertises fixed-scope specialist review, 48-hour turnaround and own client portal. Evidence of an adjacent operating alternative, not a measured product benchmark or known infrastructure.

sources.title: Stripe PayTo payment method and Connect support
sources.locator: Connect; payment properties; transaction limits and business-account coverage
sources.level: official documentation; actual merchant/bank availability untested

marketplace_assumptions.cost_scope: Execution budgets include models, connectors, compute, storage and retry allowance provisionally; not vendor-rate-derived Cloudflare totals. Provider review is Provider cost; platform exception support is separate. Monthly plan charged with domestic card and Billing rate. Platform fee refunded proportionately. Original card fees retained. No GST credit netting, additional refund/counter-dispute fees, insurance, fraud beyond modeled refunds, taxes/FX or unquoted embedded terms.

packaging_decisions.supply: One Provider business can publish multiple independently qualified Tools; one runtime can deliver multiple Tools only through per-Call isolated authority
packaging_decisions.first_commercial_proof: First template: a substantive source-cited tender compliance/evidence review sold by an existing specialist firm. One Provider, five existing recurring buyers; then a second independent Provider on the same template. Broader market direction unchanged.
packaging_decisions.progression: Measure end-to-end shaping and equal-scope delivery advantage; full-price operating renewal; second Provider reuse; an external buyer agent; then unattributed-to-founder discovery/comparison and retained marketplace purchases.
packaging_decisions.payment_choice: For invited existing clients, retain qualified Provider-issued invoice/on-account terms rather than force a new payment rail; record exact Seller credit/collection evidence. For new marketplace buyers, Stripe Connect direct AUD advance card/eligible PayTo checkout candidate. No platform trade-credit facility or multi-Provider wallet; MPP/SPT optional and geography-qualified.
packaging_decisions.preferred_pricing: Hosted A$199/month + A$5/admitted bounded review Call, ex GST; direct-client commission 0%. Existing endpoints may publish with no operating subscription, earning market-originated purchases at 15% first /5% later on-platform, disclosed at Quote. Existing direct customers stay on their existing endpoint/rail unless a separate operating benefit is demonstrated. No no-bypass tax. All pricing hypotheses, not enabled offers.

operating_assumptions.cost_scope: Monthly B2B plan and meter aggregated into one card/Billing collection. Execution/profile budgets provisional; no live runtime bill. Provider pays buyer card fees, review, rework, plan, meter, marketplace fee and modeled disputes. Platform pays execution, exception handling, per-Provider support/fixed allocation, company overhead, replacement CAC/onboarding, market buyer CAC and a gross-sale-sized expected make-good reserve. Hosted 0.1% and external-endpoint 0.01% gross-sale make-good, and 0.5% meter credit are independent hypothetical frequencies, not legal liability caps or observed failure rates. Provider benefit compares equal-volume/equal-scope existing delivery; no assumed incremental buyer demand. Net growth acquisition shown separately; all-new first month does not also pay steady-state replacement CAC. Excludes actual insurance premiums, unmodeled fraud, negotiated fees, extra dispute/refund charges and tax/FX. GST applied hypothetically; no processor tax-credit netting. Provider-owned endpoint execution is paid separately by Provider, using the same provisional execution budget conservatively; no hidden zero cost. External-endpoint acquisition/onboarding are lower hypothetical self-service costs; this is a distribution/integration complement, not the initial standalone operating business. Status-quo payment fee and payment administration are explicit zero-cost conservative assumptions, not observed bank prices. Existing endpoints receive no AE-attributed automation savings: use their existing 78-minute labor and execution on both sides. Marketplace figures normalize expected relationship purchases in steady state; no first-month buyer cash calendar is implied. Make-good reserve is not credited as Provider income before actual settlement. Endpoint mode is now free publication with market-only Calls; it cannot model direct operating sales or claim time savings. The rejected A$99 endpoint operating tier has no demonstrated incremental value and is not a launch SKU. Private invited clients may retain Provider-issued invoicing/on-account terms, with Seller-owned trade credit, confirmation and collection. Invoice sensitivity adds 0.5% bad debt after modeled refunds; no first-month Seller cash timing is implied. Zero baseline payment cost is a conservative comparison, not a free bank-transfer guarantee. Provider operating/commission expenses are ex-GST contribution inputs for a hypothetical GST-registered Provider; actual eligibility and GST cash/working-capital timing remain unqualified. Processor fees are conservatively counted at full cash amounts.
